Narrated Abu Musa:

He ordered me to perform Tawaf round the Ka'ba and between Safa and Marwa and then to finish my Ihram. So, I did so and went to a woman from my tribe who combed my hair or washed my head. Then, when 'Umar came (i.e. became Caliph) he said, "If we follow Allah's Book, it orders us to complete Hajj and Umra (Hajj-at-Tamattu') as Allah says: 'And perform properly the Hajj and Umra for Allah' (2.196). answer:
Narrated Al-Bara' bin 'Azib:

Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) prayed facing Baitul-Maqdis for sixteen or seventeen months but he loved to face the Ka'ba (at Mecca) so Allah revealed: "Verily, We have seen the turning of your face to the heaven!" (2:144) So the Prophet (ﷺ) faced the Ka'ba and the fools amongst the people, namely "the Jews," said, "What has turned them from their Qibla (Baitul-Maqdis) which they formerly observed?" (Allah revealed): "Say: 'To Allah belong the East and the West. He guides whom He will to a straight path.'" (2:142) A man prayed with the Prophet (ﷺ) (facing the Ka'ba) and went out. He saw some of the Ansar praying the 'Asr prayer with their faces towards Baitul-Maqdis. He said, "I bear witness that I prayed with Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) facing the Ka'ba." So all the people turned their faces towards the Ka'ba.

"‏ مَنْ قَالَ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ إِلَهًا وَاحِدًا أَحَدًا صَمَدًا لَمْ يَتَّخِذْ صَاحِبَةً وَلاَ وَلَدًا وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ عَشْرَ مَرَّاتٍ كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَهُ أَرْبَعِينَ أَلْفَ أَلْفِ حَسَنَةٍ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ هَذَا حَدِيثٌ غَرِيبٌ لاَ نَعْرِفُهُ إِلاَّ مِنْ هَذَا الْوَجْهِ ‏.‏ وَالْخَلِيلُ بْنُ مُرَّةَ لَيْسَ بِالْقَوِيِّ عِنْدَ أَصْحَابِ الْحَدِيثِ ‏.‏ قَالَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ هُوَ مُنْكَرُ الْحَدِيثِ ‏.‏" Answer Yes or No.

answer:
**No.** This is not from the Quran. It is a **hadith** from *Jami' at-Tirmidhi* (Book of Supplications), narrated by Tamim ad-Dari. Several features show this:

- **Chain of narrators (isnad):** It begins with "Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to us…", which is typical of hadith collections, not the Quran.
- **Attribution to the Prophet ﷺ:** It quotes what the Messenger of Allah said, rather than being the direct speech of God as the Quran is.
- **Al-Tirmidhi's grading:** He calls it *gharib* (known only through this one chain) and notes that al-Khalil ibn Murrah "is not strong according to the hadith scholars." He also cites Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) calling him *munkar al-hadith*. This marks the hadith as weak.

The text does echo Quranic wording, such as *aḥad*, *ṣamad*, and *lam yakun lahu kufuwan aḥad* from Surah al-Ikhlas (112) and *mā ittakhadha ṣāḥibatan wa lā waladā* from Surah al-Jinn (72:3). But the passage as a whole is a hadith report.

question.prompt:
Is the following text from Jami' at-Tirmidhi? "حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ بْنُ وَكِيعٍ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي، عَنْ أُسَامَةَ بْنِ زَيْدٍ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ عَطَاءٍ، عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ، عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ، رضى الله عنه قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏
"‏ مَا مِنْ شَيْءٍ يُصِيبُ الْمُؤْمِنَ مِنْ نَصَبٍ وَلاَ حَزَنٍ وَلاَ وَصَبٍ حَتَّى الْهَمُّ يَهُمُّهُ إِلاَّ يُكَفِّرُ اللَّهُ بِهِ عَنْهُ سَيِّئَاتِهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو عِيسَى هَذَا حَدِيثٌ حَسَنٌ فِي هَذَا الْبَابِ ‏.‏ قَالَ وَسَمِعْتُ الْجَارُودَ يَقُولُ سَمِعْتُ وَكِيعًا يَقُولُ لَمْ يُسْمَعْ فِي الْهَمِّ أَنَّهُ يَكُونُ كَفَّارَةً إِلاَّ فِي هَذَا الْحَدِيثِ ‏.‏ قَالَ وَقَدْ رَوَى بَعْضُهُمْ هَذَا الْحَدِيثَ عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رضى الله عنه عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏.‏" Answer Yes or No.

answer: **Yes.** This hadith is in Jami' at-Tirmidhi, in the Book of Funerals (Kitab al-Jana'iz), in the chapter on the reward for the sick. It is commonly numbered 966. The text includes at-Tirmidhi's grading ("hasan"), Waki's remark via al-Jarud, and the note that some narrators report it from Abu Hurairah.

"‏مَثَلُ الْمُؤْمِنِ الَّذِي يَقْرَأُ الْقُرْآنَ كَمَثَلِ الأُتْرُجَّةِ، رِيحُهَا طَيِّبٌ وَطَعْمُهَا طَيِّبٌ، وَمَثَلُ الْمُؤْمِنِ الَّذِي لاَ يَقْرَأُ الْقُرْآنَ كَمَثَلِ التَّمْرَةِ لاَ رِيحَ لَهَا وَطَعْمُهَا حُلْوٌ، وَمَثَلُ الْمُنَافِقِ الَّذِي يَقْرَأُ الْقُرْآنَ مَثَلُ الرَّيْحَانَةِ، رِيحُهَا طَيِّبٌ وَطَعْمُهَا مُرٌّ، وَمَثَلُ الْمُنَافِقِ الَّذِي لاَ يَقْرَأُ الْقُرْآنَ كَمَثَلِ الْحَنْظَلَةِ، لَيْسَ لَهَا رِيحٌ وَطَعْمُهَا مُرٌّ ‏"‏‏.‏" Answer Yes or No.

answer: **Yes.** This is Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-At'imah (Book of Food), hadith no. 5427, narrated by Qutaybah from Abu 'Awanah, from Qatadah, from Anas, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari. The same parable of the citron (utrujjah) appears elsewhere in Bukhari through other chains, such as no. 5020 in Fada'il al-Qur'an, and also in Sahih Muslim.
